title: Meeting for worship
hookLine: Quakers sit in silence until someone is moved to speak

lines: A PLAIN ROOM, NOBODY UP FRONT.
cards: A plain room. Benches facing each other around the walls. No pulpit, no altar, nobody up front.
People come in, sit down, and say nothing. Minutes pass. A cough.
A bench creaks. A bird outside. Then a woman near the window stands, says a few sentences about something she's been carrying, and sits down again.
Nobody answers her. The silence closes over her words like water. That's a Quaker meeting, of the kind Friends call unprogrammed.

teach.b: In an unprogrammed meeting there's no set order of service and no minister leading it. Friends gather in silence and wait on God together. That silence isn't a pause before the real thing starts.
Friends call it expectant waiting, the way you'd wait at a station for someone you know is coming.
Behind it stands a promise of Jesus, "For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them," and a line from the psalms: "Be still, and know that I am God."

When someone feels moved by the Spirit to speak, they stand and give what Friends call ministry: a few words, a verse, a memory, sometimes a song. Then they sit, and the silence returns. Nobody replies or argues.

Robert Barclay, an early Quaker writer, described coming into these silent meetings and feeling a hidden power among the people that touched his heart; as he gave way to it, the good in him was raised up.
Friends still speak of a gathered meeting, when the whole room seems to go still together.
When the hour is done, someone shakes a neighbor's hand, and the handshakes spread around the room. Not every Quaker meeting looks like this.
Programmed Friends churches have a pastor, hymns and a sermon, often with a time of open silence inside the service. Both are Quaker, and both make room to wait on God.

how: In unprogrammed Quaker meetings, Friends gather in silence and wait on God; anyone moved to speak stands and offers a few words, and the meeting closes with handshakes. Programmed Friends churches have a pastor, hymns and a sermon, often with a time of open silence.

games.q: you're sitting in an unprogrammed meeting. someone has just stood, spoken a few sentences, and sat down. what happens next?
o: others reply and discuss what was said.
the silence returns, and the words are left to settle.
a minister explains what it meant.
games.why: nobody answers or argues. the silence closes over the words, and the room keeps waiting.

practice: Sit together if someone's nearby, or alone if not, and let the room go quiet.
Don't fill the silence with a to-do list; wait, the way you'd wait for a friend at the station, and if a thought rises that seems worth keeping, hold it, then let it sink back into the quiet.
If you pray, wait on God; if you don't, simply wait and listen.

wordCard.voice: Meeting for worship. The Quaker gathering in silence, waiting on God together, where anyone may be moved to speak.

carryVoice: Your line: expectant waiting. In that room, silence isn't empty. Same time tomorrow.
